bibliographic.title: Agentic AI systems in electrical power systems engineering: current state-of-the-art and challenges
bibliographic.citation_apa: Ghosh, S., & Mittal, G. (2026). Agentic AI systems in electrical power systems engineering: Current state-of-the-art and challenges. Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence, 9, 1814651. https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2026.1814651

methodology.sample_description: Literature-based conceptual review with four detailed use-case applications in electrical power systems engineering; no empirical participant or dataset sample described in provided text
methodology.technology_context: agentic AI integrating LLM reasoning with autonomous planning and tool use; references to GenAI systems such as ChatGPT and Gemini, RAG, MCP, HITL/HOTL, and zero trust architecture in power system automation

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed hypothesis-and-theory review focused on defining and taxonomizing agentic AI and presenting power-system use cases, with recommendations for safe, reliable, and accountable deployment. It clearly engages LLMs, GenAI, RAG, and human oversight concepts, and touches regulated or high-stakes contexts such as power systems and referenced domains like healthcare and finance. However, the provided text does not center conversational systems, chatbots, or conversational governance mechanisms; governance appears as deployment accountability and failure-mode discussion rather than governance of conversational interaction. Fit to the review scope is therefore partial and borderline rather than central.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Automated triage graded the paper as a central candidate, but the available text indicates a domain-specific agentic-AI review in electrical power systems rather than explicit conversational governance in regulated LLM conversational systems.

appraisal.notes: Appropriate as a conceptual/theory paper establishing agentic-AI definitions, taxonomy, and power-system case studies. Provided excerpts do not describe systematic search methods, inclusion criteria, or reproducible literature sampling. Governance discussion is present at a high level through accountability and failure-mode recommendations, but conversational-governance mechanisms are not evidenced in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: The argument is internally coherent around agentic AI evolution, taxonomy, and power-system applications, but the supplied text offers limited transparency on review methodology and limited direct relevance to conversational governance in regulated LLM conversational systems.

coding.theme: Agentic AI governance and deployment challenges in electrical power systems
coding.subtheme: Taxonomy and accountability recommendations for LLM-enabled autonomous agents

synthesis.main_claim: Agentic AI represents a third evolutionary phase beyond classical agents and generative AI by combining LLM reasoning with autonomous planning and action, and the paper proposes a definition/taxonomy plus power-system case studies and recommendations for safe, reliable, and accountable deployment.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a conceptual and taxonomical framing of agentic AI, distinguishes it from classical and generative AI, and discusses state-of-the-art applications and deployment challenges in electrical power systems engineering.
synthesis.limitations: Based on the provided text, the work is broad and domain-specific to power systems; review methodology and conversational-governance mechanisms are not clearly specified.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as borderline supporting or contextual evidence for agentic LLM governance, human oversight terminology, RAG, and accountability in critical-infrastructure settings; not suitable as central evidence for conversational governance unless fuller text shows stronger conversational-system focus.
